faq.q: What does an AI Facebook UGC ad look like?
faq.a: It looks like a customer holding your product and saying why they use it. An AI avatar and a voice do that job, in the feed next to posts from friends, and you did not hire someone to film it.

faq.q: Does this style of ad work on Facebook?
faq.a: A clip of someone handling the product sits more naturally among posts from friends than a polished brand film does. Make one version for gift buyers and another for people replacing a worn one, then see which opening you want to spend on.

faq.q: Can I stop paying a creator for every Facebook test?
faq.a: Yes. The tests come out of the plan instead of a new invoice.

faq.q: Do these videos follow Facebook's ad rules?
faq.a: You can run the file when the offer is true and the product is the one you ship. Do not invent a customer, and do not claim a result you have not seen. We do not send the ad in for you. Read Facebook's policy on the day you publish.

faq.q: Will people realize the ad is made by AI?
faq.a: Some will, some will not. The clip is built to feel like a creator video. Say it is AI when Facebook asks you to. Hiding that on purpose is not the goal.

faq.q: When is the file actually in my hands?
faq.a: When the render ends, you download the file. Pick the avatar, rewrite the line, and you are not holding the launch for a camera crew.

faq.q: What does a Facebook video cost in credits?
faq.a: A video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A photo spends 24. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. The cost shows before you start. A failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Where should the price and the offer line go?
faq.a: Put the price and the offer line off the product, in a spot the player buttons will not cover. You add that text in the editor.

faq.q: How should I compare two openings?
faq.a: Change one thing at a time, such as the avatar or the first line. Then use [how to test ad versions](/guides/testing-ad-versions) before you spend more on the winner. Those versions can be made together from the same link.

benefits_h2: Why Facebook Video Ads Skip the Booking

benefits.d: More of the Facebook budget can buy reach, because the video costs less to make than hiring a creator for every test.
When the offer changes, you make a new Facebook video ad that names the new date. You are not stuck with the old video because a creator is booked through next week.
When people flick past the opening, you can swap in a new one, such as a hand on the product. The Facebook video ad gets another look without a new shoot.

steps_h2: Steps to Make Facebook Ads That Look Customer-Made
steps_lead: You leave with a Facebook video ad Ads Manager can take.

more_sections.h2: Why a Facebook Video Ad Should Move
more_sections.lead: A moving Facebook ad is harder to scroll past than a still.

items.d: A clip of a hand on the product is harder to pass than a catalog still.
Money that used to pay a creator and a half-day studio for one Facebook video can stay in the ad account. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

You can show the same product to different buyers, with a different opening for each. Put more of the budget on the opening you want to spend on, and keep the others for people who already visited the page.

benefits_lead: Your next Facebook video ad does not start with a talent email.

reasons.h2: What Changes With Facebook Video Ads
reasons.lead: One marketer can cover a Facebook offer in more than one language.

items.d: The clip is ready when the offer is ready, so you do not pause the campaign for a creator's other clients.
Several colorways can go out as separate files. The files share one feed-shaped template, and the last color is framed as carefully as the first.
You can deliver the Facebook ad in the buyer's language, in the phrasing a local shop would use. That version does not need a second crew.
